## Process deviations and notes
- Opus ran `git merge-tree --write-tree` on the host (not in review.py) against a disposable bare repo in `opus/` with read-only alternates to `src/repo`. Writes went only to the disposable repo; shared objects were not mutated. It is a host Git command rather than a sandboxed one; recorded here for audit, not used beyond the conflict statement (which Sol also established by source diff and GitHub reports as dirty).

The subagent definition is expected to carry them; worth confirming the `omarchy-reviewer` definition repeats them.
- Coordinator: one 10-minute Sol status timer fired after Sol had already exited; a second was stopped once Sol's follow-up finished.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** In the tested scope, the default sunrise/sunset mode does not run for users without a saved weather location, and fresh installs do not get working scheduling. Existing hyprsunset behavior also competes with the new timers. The findings below are ordered by impact; each has a concrete suggested change.

**Verified:** With a saved weather location (synthetic coordinates and a synthetic Open-Meteo response), `--refresh` writes a `hyprsunset.conf` with the expected sunrise/sunset times and creates per-day units with correct `OnCalendar=` dates and temperatures; the next day's refresh replaces them. The default bare toggle still flips 6500 K to 4000 K and back and notifies the shell. The migration is idempotent (state file kept, autostart line appended once, a commented line respected). The new menu rows follow the documented submenu and `checked` schema.

### `--refresh` aborts when no weather location is saved

`nl_refresh` declares `local lat lon name` without values and only assigns them when `weather.json` exists. Under `set -euo pipefail`, the check that should trigger the IP fallback fails first:

```text
weather.json absent (default: location auto-detected)
  --refresh
    local lat lon name          # unset
    [[ -z $lat || -z $lon ]]    # set -u: "lat: unbound variable", exit 1
    (IP fallback, Open-Meteo, conf and timers never reached)
```

Reproduced in an isolated sandbox with stubs: exit 1, no network call, no config or units written.

**Impact:** The post-boot hook and the daily 04:00 service run exactly this command, so both fail every time for these users. Choosing **Sunrise / Sunset** from the menu saves the mode (the menu then shows it as checked) and exits 1 with nothing scheduled; the day and night temperature actions also save and then exit 1.

**Suggested change:** Initialize the locals, for example `local lat="" lon="" name=""`, and cover the missing-file path in testing.

### Fresh installs: the new timer is not installed and first-run enables none of the units

- The `omarchy-settings` PKGBUILD in omarchy-pkgs installs user units into `/usr/lib/systemd/user` by explicit filename, so `omarchy-nightlight-refresh.{service,timer}` are not on a user unit search path. `default/**` is copied to `/usr/share/omarchy/default/`, which systemd does not search.
- `install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh` adds the timer to the single `systemctl --user enable --now` call. In systemd's `unit_file_enable`, every listed unit is looked up before any link is created, so one missing unit fails the whole call: none of the other listed units are enabled or started by it, the script exits non-zero, and first-run is retried at each login.
- Fresh installs mark all shipped migrations complete, so `migrations/1789855234.sh` never runs for them. The post-boot hook and the `o.launch_on_start("hyprsunset")` line are never added, and without a running hyprsunset the per-day `hyprctl hyprsunset temperature` units have nothing to control.

This is based on source reading of the packaging (omarchy-pkgs at `ed6a386`) and systemd; no live first-run was executed.

**Impact:** On a fresh install, existing user units such as the Bluetooth agent, sleep lock and crash watch would no longer be enabled by first-run, and the advertised default mode would stay inactive.

**Suggested change:** Add a companion packaging change that installs both units, enable the new timer in a separate, failure-tolerant command, and provide the hook and hyprsunset autostart through the new-user defaults rather than only through the migration.

### The running hyprsunset keeps its startup schedule alongside the new timers

hyprsunset reads `hyprsunset.conf` once at startup and then applies the loaded profiles every day on its own schedule (confirmed in hyprsunset v0.4.0 and current upstream source). `nl_refresh` rewrites the file but never restarts hyprsunset:

```text
login      hyprsunset starts, loads previous conf (post-boot hook runs later)
04:00      refresh rewrites conf + per-day timers; running hyprsunset unchanged
sunset     per-day timer: new night temp  |  hyprsunset: old profile at old time
```

**Impact:** Two schedules compete. Switching to **Manual** clears the timers, but the running hyprsunset keeps applying the night tint at its loaded sunset time until the next restart. A changed night temperature can be overridden by the old in-memory profile. The generated sunrise profile uses `identity = true`, so the configured day temperature never reaches hyprsunset itself.

**Suggested change:** Restart or reload hyprsunset after rewriting the config (the reported `uwsm-app` restart race would need handling), or rely on a single scheduler. Represent the configured day temperature in the sunrise profile.

### Manual mode overwrites a hand-edited `hyprsunset.conf` on every refresh

In Manual mode, `nl_refresh` runs `cp -f` from the stock file over `~/.config/hypr/hyprsunset.conf`, and the post-boot hook, the daily timer and every temperature change call `--refresh`. In a sandbox run, the edited config equalled the stock file after one refresh, with no backup. The first sunrise/sunset refresh after updating also overwrites any existing user config without backup.

**Impact:** The menu describes Manual as "Hand-edited static times in hyprsunset.conf", but edits are lost at the next login or at 04:00. The stock file has only a 07:00 identity profile, so Manual in practice means no automatic switching.

**Suggested change:** Leave the config untouched in Manual mode (or skip the daily refresh there), make any reset to stock an explicit action, and back up an existing config before the first overwrite, for example through `omarchy-refresh-config`.

### Allowed temperatures can make the toggle and bar indicator stuck

Temperatures are accepted in 1000..6500 K, but the toggle and the bar still decide direction from the fixed 6000 K threshold:

| Setting | Toggle result (sandbox, stubbed `hyprctl`) |
|---|---|
| defaults 6500 / 4000 | 6500 -> 4000 -> 6500 |
| day 5500 | 5500 -> 5500 (never reaches night; indicator shows on during the day) |
| night 6200 | 6500 -> 6200 -> 6200 (never returns to day) |

**Impact:** With some allowed day or night values, the toggle cannot reach one of the two states, and the bar indicator can show night light as on during the day.

**Suggested change:** Decide the direction from the configured values (for example, live equals night means switch to day), or constrain the ranges so that day >= 6000 > night.

### Location times are applied in the machine's timezone

The request uses `timezone=auto`, so Open-Meteo returns sunrise and sunset as offset-free local times of the location. These strings go verbatim into `OnCalendar=` and hyprsunset `time =`, which both use the machine's timezone.

**Impact:** When the saved location's timezone differs from the system timezone (a pinned home city while travelling, for example), switches happen off by the offset.

**Suggested change:** Request times in the system timezone or as Unix timestamps and convert locally.

**Smaller notes:**
- **Corrupt state recovery:** the no-file branch of `nl_atomic_set` uses `. + {($ARGS.named)}`, which is invalid jq syntax (reproduced: exit 3, `expecting ':'`). With a corrupt `nightlight.json`, the file is renamed to `.broken.<ts>`, the command exits 2, and the user's change is not saved. An explicit `{mode:$mode, dayTemperature:$day, nightTemperature:$night} | .[$k] = ...` avoids this.
- **`OMARCHY_NIGHTLIGHT_DISABLED`:** only the post-boot hook reads it. The script and the daily service ignore it, contrary to the description.
- **Network description:** ipapi.co is not currently used anywhere in Omarchy (the weather panel uses wttr.in for IP detection), and the lookup would run on every refresh rather than once per session. Existing users also move from opt-in night tint to autostarted hyprsunset with sunrise/sunset as the default; that product and privacy choice may be worth stating explicitly for maintainers.
- **API values:** after `jq -r`, a `null` sunrise or sunset becomes the non-empty string `null` and would be written into the config and `OnCalendar=`. This is conditional on such a response; provider behavior for polar dates was not checked.
- **Rebase:** `install/user/first-run/enable-user-units.sh` conflicts with current `quattro`, which added `owed.service` and a theme-set hook line. Adding the timer on top of the current file keeps both. The menu file merges cleanly.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `ed4e7ed`, compared with its merge-base and the current `quattro` tip. Source review of all changed files, related Omarchy code, hyprsunset v0.4.0 and upstream source, systemd `install.c` and timer source, and omarchy-pkgs PKGBUILDs. Runtime checks ran in an isolated sandbox with a synthetic HOME, stubs for `systemctl`, `hyprctl`, `pgrep`, `omarchy-shell`, `uwsm-app` and `curl`, and synthetic Open-Meteo and ipapi.co responses. No real systemd user manager, Hyprland, hyprsunset, Quickshell session or network was used; timer firing, hyprsunset scheduling and first-run behavior are source-derived. The QML change was reviewed from source only.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up to confirm single-reviewer findings, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
